title: Why Did My HVAC UV Light Stop Working?
h1: Why Do HVAC UV Lights Stop Working?
description: HVAC UV lights usually stop working because the bulb aged out, the ballast failed or a safety switch cut power. Here are the common causes and what to check.
quick_answer: Most HVAC UV lights stop working because the bulb reached the end of its life, the ballast or power supply failed, a safety switch cut power, or a breaker or connection lost power. A bulb can also keep glowing after it has stopped putting out much UV, so a lit bulb isn't proof it's still working.
body:
UV lights in HVAC systems are installed near the indoor coil or in the ductwork to help keep mold and bacteria from growing on damp surfaces. They work quietly, so most people don't notice when they stop. Often the first clue is a viewing window that's gone dark, a musty smell returning or a reminder that it's been a while since the bulb was changed.

What are the most common reasons a UV light stops working?

  • The bulb has reached the end of its life. UV bulbs lose output over time. Many manufacturers recommend replacing them about once a year, even if they still glow.
  • The ballast or power supply failed. The ballast powers the bulb. If it fails, the bulb won't light even if the bulb itself is fine.
  • A safety switch is open. Many units have a switch that cuts power when the cover or access panel is opened. If the panel isn't seated properly, the light stays off.
  • Power loss. A tripped breaker, a loose plug, a switched outlet that got turned off or a loose wire can all cut power.
  • A dirty or coated bulb. Dust and film on the bulb block UV output, so the light runs but does little.
  • Heat or moisture damage. Units installed in hot attics or near condensation can wear out faster.

Why is the bulb glowing but the light isn't working?

The visible blue or violet glow you see isn't the same as the UV-C light that does the work. As a bulb ages, its UV output drops even though it still lights up. So a bulb can look fine while doing very little. That's why replacing on a schedule matters more than whether it looks lit.

What can I safely check myself?

A few checks are fine for most homeowners:

  1. Check whether the unit has an indicator light or viewing window and whether it's lit.
  2. Check the breaker panel for a tripped breaker.
  3. If the unit plugs in, make sure the plug is fully seated and the outlet works.
  4. Look at the access panel near the UV unit to make sure it's closed tightly, since a loose panel can trip the safety switch.
  5. Check when the bulb was last replaced. Many people write the date on the unit.

Never look directly at a working UV-C bulb, and don't run it with the cover off. UV-C light can harm your eyes and skin. Turn off power to the unit before touching the bulb.

Can I replace the UV bulb myself?

Some units are designed for homeowner bulb changes, and the manufacturer's instructions explain the steps. If yours is one of them, turn off power, let the bulb cool, wear gloves so skin oils don't get on the new bulb, and handle the old one carefully. UV bulbs contain a small amount of mercury, so don't toss a broken bulb in household trash. Follow local disposal guidance.

If the light still won't come on with a new bulb, the problem is likely the ballast, the wiring or the switch. That's electrical work inside the HVAC system and should be handled by a technician.

How do I keep a UV light working?

  • Replace the bulb on the manufacturer's schedule, often yearly.
  • Have the bulb wiped clean during maintenance visits.
  • Keep the HVAC filter fresh so less dust reaches the bulb.
  • Have the ballast and wiring checked during your annual tune-up.

What else can look like a UV light failure?

Sometimes the light is fine and the problem is elsewhere. A musty smell can come back because of a clogged condensate drain, a dirty filter or high indoor humidity, not a dead bulb. A technician can check the bulb, the coil and the drain together so you're not replacing parts that still work.

Is a UV light worth fixing?

For many homes, yes. Our coastal humidity and long cooling seasons inland mean the indoor coil stays damp for long stretches, and a working UV light helps keep it cleaner. That can mean fewer musty smells and a coil that stays more efficient.

faqs: How long do HVAC UV bulbs last?
Many manufacturers recommend replacing the bulb about once a year. UV output fades over time even if the bulb still glows, so check your unit's instructions and replace it on that schedule.
How do I know if my HVAC UV light is working?

Many units have an indicator light or a small viewing window. If it's dark, the bulb, ballast or power is out. If it's lit but the bulb is past its replacement date, it may not be putting out much useful UV.
Is it safe to look at an HVAC UV light?
No. Don't look directly at a working UV-C bulb, and don't run it with the cover off. Use the viewing window or indicator light, and turn off power before handling the bulb.
Do UV lights replace air filters?
No. UV lights help keep the coil and nearby surfaces cleaner, but they don't capture dust, pollen or dander. You still need a good filter, changed on schedule.
